💡 Key Takeaways
  • Effective immediately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors just voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, CEO and board director — just 11 days after he resigned amid an explosive espionage and extramarital affair scandal, and a mere six days after the manufacturer insisted it had no intention of bringing him back.
  • If you blinked over the last two weeks, you might have missed the entire post-Jensen Huang era of Nvidia.
  • So what changed between last Tuesday’s firm “no” and this morning’s unanimous “welcome back”?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Effective immediately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors just voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, CEO and board director — just 11 days after he resigned amid an explosive espionage and extramarital affair scandal, and a mere six days after the manufacturer insisted it had no intention of bringing him back.

If you blinked over the last two weeks, you might have missed the entire post-Jensen Huang era of Nvidia. It is the kind of corporate whiplash that makes Sam Altman’s infamous five-day OpenAI ousting look like PTO. To make sense of how the world’s most consequential chipmaker pulled off a full-speed reverse, you have to look at the sheer chaos of the last 25 days.

So what changed between last Tuesday’s firm “no” and this morning’s unanimous “welcome back”?

Industry observers note that according to Nvidia’s official announcement, two things broke the deadlock: a series of sitdowns where the board became “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead,” and — crucially — a green light from Washington.

The board explicitly noted that it “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

Combine that quiet federal clearance with an internal employee revolt, vocal backing from the White House and a brutal month on the stock ticker, and the board’s math became pretty simple.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Jones stated in Monday’s statement, thanking Colette Kress for holding the fort as interim CEO before returning to her full-time CFO duties.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Huang, for his part, struck a notably humbler tone than the usual keynote bravado I’ve seen in person a few times.

Sources indicate that "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment... Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work." — Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO.

Recent findings suggest that before you get too excited with “WE ARE SO BACK” responses and “stonks” GIFs, read the fine print at the bottom of Nvidia’s press release. Huang may have his title back, but he’s walking back into a very different corporate structure — and the legal storm hasn’t magically evaporated:.

If you were hoping that two weeks of boardroom chaos at Nvidia would pop the AI bubble and magically bring back $90 DDR5 kits (like me), I have some bad news: Jensen Huang’s comeback just put the AI infrastructure train right back at full throttle.

With Wall Street cheering his return and Washington clearing the runway, hyperscalers aren’t tapping the brakes on data center spending anytime soon.

That means Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron have zero reason to pull wafers off high-margin data center memory and send them back to everyday PC builders — especially with Trendforce expecting DRAM prices to climb another 10-15% this quarter and stay tight well into 2027.

It has been revealed that does that mean the dream of RAMageddon dying is gone? Not quite — it just changes your game initiative.

If you see a legitimate Black Friday deal that actually undercuts pre-crisis pricing, treat it like an escape hatch. Waiting for “cheaper RAM next spring” is a gamble that’s looking worse by the hour.

There is one genuine silver lining. While DRAM stays squeezed, Trendforce’s latest forecast demonstrates NAND flash prices finally turning the corner and starting to dip as early as Q1 2027 — so unless you spot a genuinely fair Black Friday deal, don’t let retailers gouge you on storage right now.

Nvidia’s rebound might keep AI demand humming, but it doesn’t bail the memory giants out of their California antitrust lawsuit or stop the mainstream backlash over inflated PC prices.

According to recent reports, jensen getting his desk back is great news for Nvidia shareholders. For the rest of us just trying to buy a computer without paying an absurd memory tax, the message is simple: grab the real Black Friday bargains while they exist, ignore the fake red discount stickers, and buckle in — RAMageddon isn’t packing its bags just yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Big Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the firm is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

It has been revealed that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, said in 2023 that the company’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

Meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the firm states. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

Industry observers note that take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its latest data center designs compared to its original ones.

But, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The firm also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”.

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
  • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

Recent findings suggest that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

It has been revealed that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

Sources indicate that the Treasury Department stated last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the aims.

According to recent reports, last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

According to recent reports, long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

"Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold said in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah remarked. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

Industry observers note that the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah remarked. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Recent findings suggest that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah remarked in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Sources indicate that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh noted in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder noted.

"The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

In a recent development, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving enhancement. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

Recent findings suggest that the v26.45 upgrade concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch owners can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Recent findings suggest that also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?

Constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how promptly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The update improves battery life without consumers having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

In a recent development, that’s not the only Google Play Services update that Wear OS smartwatch consumers can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov.
  • Shares hit a record close of about $292 (split-adjusted) on June 25, so they're off about 73% from there.
  • What could those 63 shares be worth at the end of 2030?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 23, 2026 at 9:23AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Sandisk ›.

With an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov. 19, shares of flash memory maker Sandisk (SNDK +14.22%) closed at about $79 on Nov. 20 on a split-adjusted basis (about $630 in pre-split terms). At that price, $5,000 buys about 63 shares.

Shares hit a record close of about $292 (split-adjusted) on June 25, so they're off about 73% from there.

What could those 63 shares be worth at the end of 2030? My estimate is around $8,800. That'd be a return of about 75%, or almost 15% a year.

Getting there doesn't require flash prices to keep rising. In fact, my estimate assumes Sandisk's earnings in 2030 are around half of what it's earning today. It also assumes investors value those earnings at about the same price-to-earnings multiple they paid for the stock as recently as September.

Sandisk's profits keep climbing, but the growth is slowing every quarter. On a split-adjusted basis, its non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share went from around $2.93 in fiscal Q3 of 2026 to $4.91 in fiscal Q4, a 68% sequential leap. For fiscal Q1 of 2027 (the quarter ended Oct. 2, 2026), the number hit $6.19 -- up 26% sequentially and up from around $0.15 a year before. And management's guidance for fiscal Q2 calls for $6.88 to $7.13, which would be about 13% growth at the midpoint.

Sources indicate that that fiscal Q2 midpoint comes to about $28 a share in a full year. At around $79, the stock trades at under 3 times that earnings pace.

In other words, the market seems to expect these earnings to drop a lot.

Sources indicate that investors weren't always so skeptical. When Sandisk closed at around $224 (split-adjusted) on Sept. 18, the stock traded at about 10 times the annualized adjusted earnings per share Sandisk had just guided for fiscal Q1.

Recent findings suggest that chinese cloud companies cutting orders, consumer devices shipping with less memory, and upcoming production capacity coming online could tip the flash memory market into oversupply in 2027, according to a Nov. 18 bulletin from research firm TrendForce.

It has been revealed that and Sandisk's results can drop fast when prices turn. Its adjusted earnings per share for all of fiscal 2025, which ended in late June 2025, came to around $0.37 on a split-adjusted basis. That full-year number is less than the company expects to earn in one week this quarter.

Industry observers note that to be fair, Sandisk is a bigger and different business than it was then. Its datacenter revenue hit $4.8 billion in fiscal Q1, versus just $269 million in the year-earlier quarter, and it now makes up over 40% of total revenue.

But a business tied so closely to flash prices is unlikely to hold today's earnings through a full downturn.

For fiscal 2030 (which ends in mid-2030), I'll assume adjusted earnings per share of around $14. That number is half today's guided pace -- but still about 58% over the $8.86 a share Sandisk earned in fiscal 2026, after adjusting for the split.

NASDAQ · As of 11:48 AM ET 11/23/26.

According to recent reports, at about 10 times earnings (about what the market paid on guided earnings in September), $14 a share works out to a stock price of about $140 by the end of 2030. Sixty-three shares at $140 would be worth about $8,800. From around $79, the gain is almost 15% a year over about four years.

I'm also keeping the share count flat, which arguably makes the estimate conservative. Sandisk repurchased $5.0 billion of shares in fiscal Q1 alone, and any more buybacks might raise earnings per share above my assumption.

Industry observers note that then again, the estimate may also be too high. If fiscal 2030 earnings came in at a quarter of today's pace instead (around $7 a share), the same 10 times earnings would put the stock at about $70. The $5,000 would drop to about $4,400.

In a recent development, in the end, I think about $8,800 is a fair estimate for $5,000 invested in Sandisk today, if the next flash downturn is over by 2030. That's a solid return, and it doesn't rely on the boom lasting.

Industry observers note that with the stock seemingly priced for a deeper slump than the one I'm assuming, I think shares are worth a look at around $79. Given how broad the range of outcomes is, I'd limit them to a small slice of a diversified portfolio.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message.
  • In a recent development, the privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data.
  • According to recent reports, that threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

In a recent development, the privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data. In a blog post announcing the change, Signal President Meredith Whittaker said these AI bots scan what’s on your screen to get to know you, capturing your data and making it available to AI systems to fulfill your requests, such as answering questions you may ask.

According to recent reports, that threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote. So it’s putting a stop to it with a default setting to block screenshots in the Signal app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture information on Android screens by default.

Whittaker said that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the firm is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

Industry observers note that the problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal says that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

“Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” Whittaker wrote.

Industry observers note that whittaker stated the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how big tech AI agents work.

In a recent development, “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker mentioned. “This is also the reason we are at the moment unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”.

In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

“So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” noted Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”.

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

Strand noted the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand said.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 19, much-anticipated AI giant Anthropic (ANT -2.34%) finally became available to regular retail traders through the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history. The listing valued shares at $83 each. That valuation gave Anthropic an eye-popping market cap of just under $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. By the close of the first day of trading, its valuation reached $1.76 trillion, putting it in the Top-10 among the world's most valuable companies (by the weekend, the valuation had fallen to $1.65 trillion on a fully diluted basis). Without full dilution, the valuation is closer to $1.2 trillion, which still makes it a very valuable company.

According to recent reports, clearly, huge expectations are already baked into Anthropic's current valuation. That leaves potential new investors wondering how much room is left for continued stock price growth over the long term. Let's dig into the pros and cons of the stock to decide if it is a compelling buy.

NASDAQ · As of 11:49 AM ET 11/23/26.

Recent findings suggest that in late 2022, OpenAI released its groundbreaking large language model (LLM) ChatGPT, which wowed the market with its ability to answer user queries with humanlike speech patterns. Anthropic had been founded a year earlier with a very similar business model. But the company distinguished itself by an apparent emphasis on safety, coupled with a major push into the business-to-business side of the opportunity.

Industry observers note that anthropic's flagship LLM, Claude, has increasingly become the go-to solution for enterprise clients who want to use AI models to automate their internal workflows, code, and analyze large volumes of data. A study from Menlo Ventures has found that the model has already captured 55% of enterprise LLM spending, putting it far ahead of OpenAI's 31%.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic's success is showing up in its financial results, with its S-1 filing reporting $16.3 billion in revenue for the six months ended June 30. That's an eye-popping 1,300% jump from the prior-year period, and management seems extremely optimistic about the future.

According to recent reports, anthropic CEO Dario Amodei remarked he believes AI technology could continue to improve exponentially, eventually reaching a level where one data center can be compared to a "country of geniuses in a datacenter" capable of revolutionizing every human endeavor. This would include curing diseases like cancer and Alzheimer's. If things go as expected, the economic effects could be life-changing for early investors who buy shares before these things potentially happen.

Industry observers note that at this point, there are few people who still doubt the potential power of generative AI (although most of us probably aren't as bullish as Anthropic's leadership). That said, a promising technology doesn't necessarily guarantee a profitable business model. We saw this during the dot-com bubble, when many early internet companies quickly failed, even though the internet as a technology has been a lasting success.

Sources indicate that there are some early warning signs in Anthropic's S-1 filing. While revenue growth is explosive, the company generated a staggering net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, compared to just under $13 billion in the prior-year period.

Sources indicate that the good news is that most of this was due to a one-time $72.4 billion charge related to changes in the fair value of financial instruments issued to early investors. As Anthropic's valuation has grown, so has the estimated value of these obligations, resulting in a massive accounting loss. The good news is that this is not a cash outflow. Still, it can lead to substantial shareholder dilution as convertible notes are converted into additional units of stock, increasing the number of shares outstanding.

In a recent development, anthropic is an expensive stock. With a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of around 170, it trades at a substantial premium to the S&P 500 average of 18. While this is somewhat understandable given the company's explosive growth rate, it leaves plenty of downside risk if things don't go as expected.

There are also growing fears that AI itself is a bubble that won't generate enough revenue to justify the hundreds of billions right now being spent on data center equipment. So while Anthropic definitely belongs on your investment watch list, it may make more sense to wait for the dust to settle before actually buying the stock.

In a recent development, after reviewing close to 100 coffee makers in the last 5 years, we've yet to find a machine that can beat the formidable Technivorm Moccamaster KBGV Select. Durable, consistent and iconic for a reason, it's back at the top of our guide after we re-reviewed it in early 2026.

If you're looking for a great espresso machine, it's the De'Longhi La Specialista Touch we recommend above all others. It has been revealed that I've been reviewing coffee makers for over six years, and I never log on for a day of work without two shots of espresso in my system. An SCA-certified barista, I've tested everything from a $9 French press to a $3,000 espresso machine. I'd happily drink a brew made in any of the seven machines I've featured in my carefully-curated list of the best coffee makers. So if you want an expert-approved brewer, just keep scrolling.

In a recent development, it's late November, which means Black Friday deals are live. Our on-page tech in this guide will show you when there are discounts on our favorite machines, but if you're looking for more coffee deals over the holiday season, we're continually updating our roundup of the best Black Friday deals, including coffee makers like the Keurig K-Express which is almost half price right now. Or, if you're after inspiration for the enthusiast in your life, these are the best gifts for coffee lovers this holiday season.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

It has been revealed that we've reviewed nearly a dozen coffee makers so far this year, and most notably, reviewer Erin re-tested the iconic Moccamaster, which we last put through its paces back in 2021. We wanted to see if it still held its own against the many outstanding releases of the last few years. And the answer is a resounding yes. Now back at the top of our guide, it's certainly the one to beat for the rest of the year's top releases.

Compiling this buying guide has required a lot of evaluation and comparison between completely unrelated methods of brewing, as well as machines that span from $50 to well over $2,000. How, you might wonder, can we rank these machines if they're being tested against completely different criteria?

It's true, I'd never tell you to buy a drip coffee maker if you love espresso, and we'd never tell you to buy the most premium machine if you're on a budget, so before you buy, you need to have a rough idea of what kind of coffee you actually want to make at home.

Recent findings suggest that in this guide, I've included drip coffee makers, as well as a range of single-serve machines and espresso machines. And when ranking these products, I've considered what's right for most people. I know a lot more about coffee than the majority of buyers, so I had to go back to basics when writing this guide to make it accessible to everyone.

It has been revealed that even within the Tom's Guide team, there's a huge range of coffee preferences. There are some people who would turn their nose up at a cup of pod coffee, and would never consider straying from their carefully evaluated coffee setup.

In a recent development, for others, coffee is simply a tool for waking up in the morning, and you just want a reliable and space-efficient gadget to fill your cup with something cheaper and better than the stuff you'd get from a chain coffee shop. That's ok too, because you know your budget, and you know what you're looking for. And no matter what it is that you're seeking, I'm confident that I've included it in this guide.

Each and every machine has been hand-selected and tested by myself or one of Tom's Guide's expert testers, so you can click through to read full, detailed reviews before you make up your mind.

Sources indicate that the Technivorm Moccamaster KBGV Select has been in this buying guide for five years, but a lot has changed since our first review in 2021. So in early 2026, we took it for another spin to see if it can hold its own against the latest and greatest releases.

Well, the results are in, and the Moccamaster is still the cream of the crop. Hand-made in the Netherlands, the brand has a well-deserved reputation for quality construction and dependable results. It's not the cheapest option, but if you treat it with care, it will last a lifetime.

According to recent reports, reviewer Erin mentioned "the Moccamaster is so famous because nothing really compares. Nothing comes close. The Moccamaster has been topping “best-of” lists before best-of lists were even a thing — it’s reigned supreme since the ‘60s.".

Sources indicate that compared to feature-rich options like the Ratio Four, Breville Luxe Brewer, or OXO Brew 8-Cup, the Moccamaster stands out for its simplicity and efficiency. It forgoes extras like cold brew modes or app controls, but it’s faster than the Ratio Four, easier to use than the Breville Luxe Brewer, and delivers a more consistent cup than the OXO. The machine offers simplicity and ease of use in everyday drip brewing.

To use, simply add your water to the tank and your grounds to the filter, and switch it on. However, it's this simplicity that has earned special recognition from the Specialty Coffee Association. Using a copper heating element and precise brew temperature control, the KBGV Select can hit industry-standard temperatures between 196°F and 205°F in under a minute and, crucially, stay there throughout the entire brewing process. The gentle showerhead-style water dispenser will evenly agitate coffee grounds to create a balanced extraction.

According to recent reports, the Breville Bambino Plus has been on the market for seven years, but it's still one of the most popular espresso machines ever released. If you're based in Europe (like me) you'll know this brand as Sage, but the machines are otherwise the same.

With groundbreaking automatic steaming technology, which is still top of the line nearly a decade later, this is the espresso machine for you if you're in the market for an entry-level machine with some serious power.

We made some outstanding shots of espresso with this gadget. I'm talking drool-worthy toffee-colored strands of crema and a vibrant extraction that tasted fantastic. You should note, this machine doesn't have a grinder built in.

You'll want to pair it with one of the best coffee grinders (you can buy a good one for around $100, and our reviews walk you through all the options) for the ideal espresso, but if you use a double-walled portafilter you can still achieve a lively brew when using pre-ground coffee.

Industry observers note that as for the automatic milk steaming, this thing can achieve a very fine micro-foam that's totally latte art-worthy, completely hands-free. And it automatically purges after each use, which will keep the steam wand clog-free and running smoothly (so long as you descale regularly).

If you want a single-serve coffee maker that can truly do it all, you should look no further than the Nespresso Vertuo Lattissima. Featuring a separate milk dispenser that offers milk-only drinks and two lengths of milk add-ins to any coffee size you opt for, the beauty of this machine is in its simplicity.

You can simply store the milk dispenser in the refrigerator when it's not in use, and you'll get the joys of the entirety of Nespresso's six-size Vertuo system if you prefer a long black coffee or an espresso to start the day.

Recent findings suggest that we enjoyed the thoughtful touches such as an adjustable cup holder to work with any beverage size, and the ability to rinse out the milk dispenser after each use. We did wish that there were more than one milk froth level available, because if you prefer a firmer layer to make an espresso or a softer latte-style steamed milk, you won't be able to adjust this using the Nespresso.

According to recent reports, because this machine is part of the Vertuo line it will automatically brew the optimum drink length for each drink and you can enjoy an ever-evolving list of capsules to mix up your routine. We even tried a cold-brew capsule, which was impressively realistic.

Sometimes, simple is better. The OXO Brew 8-Cup is one such machine. It's shy on buttons and limited on features, but this machine undeniably makes tasty coffee, and it's SCA-certified to prove it.

You can brew either 2-4 cups or 5-8 cups with the OXO Brew. It simply requires you to fill up the water tank to your desired cup amount, load up a filter and coffee grounds, then hit start.

Industry observers note that there's beauty in the simplicity, though. Its rainshower distribution ensures that grounds are soaked evenly and consistently before extraction, meaning you won't be left with anemic or muddy coffee, and your coffee will never taste burnt from uncontrolled water temperatures.

Recent findings suggest that another plus is the double-walled carafe. This will keep your brew hot for a couple of hours, making it ideal for busy households. Reviewer Camryn's only complaint was the water tank, which can't be removed. That's annoying, but it's nothing a jug can't fix.

It has been revealed that somehow, the De'Longhi La Specialista Touch manages to be both super-smart and aesthetically pleasing, while also compact enough for small kitchens. It's no mean feat, and one that won the machine the top spot in our best espresso machine buying guide.

The main addition is the responsive 3.5-inch touchscreen, which walks you through everything from dialing in your beans (finding the right grind size for your specific brew) to automatically steaming the milk for the drink of your choosing.

While there are plenty of excellent automatic features here, this machine also lets you take the reins, which will be a welcome feature for those who want to work on their home barista skills. I enjoyed hand-steaming with this machine, and was able to toggle with finer features to really master every espresso.

Industry observers note that it's a small feature, but De'Longhi should take a bow for how compact the La Specialista Touch is. It slotted easily onto my countertops, which often look drowned by larger coffee makers. And despite its compact size, it still does literally everything you could want from an espresso machine.

While it looks like a drip coffee maker, the Ratio Four is actually an automated pour-over coffee maker. So if you love pour-over, but don't love the laborious process of brewing it, the Ratio Four is for you.

With a sleek, minimalist appearance and straightforward operation, the Ratio took just under seven minutes to brew a 20-ounce serving of coffee, and one cup was complete in three and a half minutes.

In a recent development, reviewer Erin recommends this option for serious coffee lovers. She called it "sophisticated enough to excite even the most fastidious coffee shop hipster," noting that "if you’re familiar with coffee bean varieties and the phrases “pre-infusion” and “optimal flow rate” don’t scare you off, this is the machine for you.".

The main downside of this brewer is its lack of 'keep warm' setting. Unlike your average drip brewer, it's not designed with bulk brewing in mind. This one's for the true coffee enthusiasts, who would never dream of reheating a precious V60 brew. If you do want a keep-warm option, check out the Moccamaster or Breville Luxe.

Recent findings suggest that the Terra Kaffe Demi is a standout choice for those who want café-quality drinks at home with zero fuss. Its intuitive interface and one-touch operation make espresso simple, so you can enjoy impressive coffee without mastering barista skills or fiddling with settings.

There are downsides to superautomatic espresso machines, which is why few have scored highly in our rigorous Barista-led testing. But where the locked-away grinding, brewing and steaming mechanisms may feel restrictive for coffee enthusiasts, if your key concern is reliability and ease of use, you can't go wrong with the likes of the Terra Kaffe.

Industry observers note that machines that require manual tamping or careful monitoring, such as the De'Longhi La Specialista Touch, can't match the Demi's ease of use. Simply press a button, add your beans, and it will craft anything from a piping hot espresso to a long black Americano in minutes. There's one major con: it doesn't have a milk frother, which many superautomatic machines from the likes of Jura and De'Longhi do offer.

In a recent development, for anyone who wants the easiest possible coffee routine, the Demi’s accessible cleaning features are a relief. After a month of daily use, review Dan found maintenance practically painless. Pop out the brew group for a rinse, and you’re done. If you want hands-off, great-tasting espresso with minimal upkeep, the Demi delivers. But if you're a coffee lover who knows their arabica from their robusta, its lack of customisation may prove frustrating.

Sources indicate that I joined Tom's Guide in 2024 on the product reviews team. While I test everything from keyboards to vacuum cleaners, I'm also a former barista with years and years of experience, which is why I'm Tom's Guide's go-to coffee maker tester.

According to recent reports, I've tested a number of leading espresso machines from Smeg and KitchenAid, as well as other brewing methods such as the AeroPress. I've also been down to Smeg and La Pavoni HQ to get hands-on with some high-tech gear.

I’m Tom’s Guide's Reviews Editor and I’ve been an espresso enthusiast for almost a decade now.

As a former chef, I started using commercial espresso machines to make tiramisu while working in an Italian restaurant, and that’s where my fascination with 9-bar pressure began. And it hasn’t stopped since.

These days, I spend large chunks of my day testing out the latest and greatest coffee gear, from coffee grinders and weighing scales through to pour-over drippers and, of course, coffee machines.

In a recent development, at the end of the day, the most vital sign of a good coffee maker comes down to that all-important taste test. So it goes without saying that I taste a lot of coffee when putting together my coffee maker reviews. However, there are endless factors that can determine the flavor of your finished coffee, so there are some metrics I need to consider (and keep consistent) when testing coffee makers and curating buying guides.

In a recent development, the most sustainable choice you can make when buying a latest coffee maker is opting for a machine that will last for years and years. That mentioned, it's a good sign when a coffee maker comes in recyclable, sustainable packaging that still keeps it secure during shipping, so I'm always looking out for this when evaluating my first impressions of a product.

In my experience, a more drawn-out setup process can be worth the extra hassle. Some coffee makers have a water hardness strip included to input the limescale level in your water. This test takes a few extra minutes, but inputting this information will ensure the machine reminds you to descale it as and when needed to prolong its lifespan.

If a coffee maker comes with an app or any bespoke programming such as personalized profiles or pre-set timers, we troubleshoot this in testing to make sure you're getting an easy-to-use machine from the very first use.

Sources indicate that coffee makers don't have to be expensive — especially if you're buying a single-serve or drip coffee maker, but it's often the case that you get what you pay for with coffee makers. When testing I evaluate if this is the case. Does a $1,000+ coffee maker really warrant the price tag, and most importantly, would I recommend it to a friend or family member who was shopping for a newly introduced machine?

Your cup of coffee can only be as good as the grounds you use, so when testing, I try and opt for an accessible consumer blend and stick to this brand across models to ensure that the differences we taste in our coffee come from the quality of the machine, and not the beans.

Sources indicate that as a basic rule, I use fresh-roasted arabica beans in every review. This allows the taste and extraction of every coffee to shine through. And while I don't expect that every home tester will be splashing out on artisan beans, at least this way you know you're getting a machine that can create some seriously tasty coffee if you ever decide to level up from those kilo bags of robusta.

It has been revealed that this is particularly important for drip coffee makers. I test the temperature of each carafe I make when it's first brewed, and then after one hour, to test the quality of the heating plate on each machine.

Industry observers note that if freshly brewed coffee comes out too hot, it's a sign that the machine has scorched the grounds in testing, which will result in a more bitter flavor and is a sign of a poorly-made machine. Likewise, if the coffee is not hot enough, you won't get a fully developed flavor and your coffee will be weak and acidic.

Some coffee makers come with in-built grinders, so I put them through a similar process to our standalone reviews for the best coffee grinders. This involves testing the variety of grind sizes available, and how suitable this is for the type of coffee maker you're using. If your espresso maker's grinder creates great grounds for filter coffee, that's not much help!

I use a coffee sifter called Kruve to see how consistent the coffee grounds are in size and texture, and we also test coffee grinders for static.

Recent findings suggest that if an espresso machine comes with a hand milk steamer, there is an inevitable margin for user error when testing. Fortunately, I have a team of expert testers on-hand who have steamed more than a few lattes in their time, so if they find fault with a steamer, I can confidently say it's a flaw in design.

When steaming milk, I look for a smooth and fine micro-foam that doesn't burn the milk before we're able to get the consistency we want.

Some machines come with automatic frothers, and while it's hard for these to recreate a hand-steaming effect, I look for how easy they are to use and how close they come to the real thing.

If all of this seems a bit overwhelming, we've tried to simplify the category a bit and help you decide on which type of coffee maker you should buy.

We test a lot of coffee makers. It feels like there's always a new innovation to put through its paces, so our testing team can be found reliably caffeinated on any given day.

We return most of the coffee makers we test due to the high value of these machines, but on the occasion that we're allowed to keep one, we continue to test them from home in order to evaluate the value for money over time, and compare our old faithfuls to recent releases.

It has been revealed that not every coffee maker can make the list though. Here are some of the models we've recently tried.

The xBloom is one of the most interesting drip coffee makers on the market, with legions of fans who love getting involved with every step of the brewing process.

Industry observers note that let's just say Erin did not enjoy the Gevi. Its in-built grinder is really, really bad, which means it's impossible to get a decent brew out of this machine.

Smeg EMC02 Mini Pro Manual Espresso Machine (★★★★☆).

Sources indicate that smeg teamed up with La Pavoni, makers of the original espresso machine, to create the EMC02. And it lives up to the hype. In testing, Erin found that it's the closest she's got to professional equipment at home.

Industry observers note that erin described the De'Longhi Rivelia as a coffee-making robot. This superautomatic does it all, from grinding your beans to order to frothing just the right amount of milk for your desired drink. Its smart interface is what sets it apart, with different user profiles allowing you to interact with the machine depending on everything from your go-to drink to the time of day. Nespresso Vertuo Pop Plus (★★★★☆).

There's only so good Nespresso coffee can taste, so you may as well get one of the brand's cheaper machines, especially if you're not concerned with milk-based drinks. Breville Oracle Dual Boiler (★★★★☆).

Industry observers note that the Oracle Dual Boiler is Breville's latest, and dare we say, greatest release. It's massively expensive: $3,000, which makes it a tough machine to recommend. This superpowered brewer offers pro-level specs, but reviewer Pete didn't love the grinder.

Keurig K-Duo Hot & Iced (★★★★☆).

You won't find a Keurig in this guide. Compared to the myriad options on the market, I just couldn't bring myself to recommend this restrictive and bitterly dark-roasted coffee brand to the average shopper. But some people love Keurig, and we've got a dedicated best Keurig coffee maker guide just for those people. The K-Duo Hot & Iced is the winner in that guide, scoring a 4.5-star review.

Philips Barista Brew Espresso Machine (★★★☆☆).

Sources indicate that the Philips Barista Brew is the brand's latest innovation: a semi-automatic machine that features a separate grinder and brewing unit. In testing we were very impressed with the espresso we made in this machine, but the milk steaming was lacking.

This super-smart coffee makers is one of the niftiest and quietest machines we've tested, but the eye-watering price tag means we'd struggle to recommend it to most people. There’s nothing like a great cup of coffee to wake you up in the morning, so if you’re looking to invest in a fresh coffee maker, you’ll want one that makes the ideal brew, provides the functionality and practicality you desire and comes in on budget. Here are a few things you’ll need to think about.

Sources indicate that will it fit?A coffee maker sits on the countertop, so measure the space where you proposal to keep the machine before you buy one. Be sure to determine the clearance between the countertop and the bottom of your cabinets. Most, but not all coffee makers will fit under a cabinet.

It has been revealed that coffee qualityIf you're passionate about coffee, look for a brewer that states it meets the Specialty Coffee Association's Golden Cup Standard. This means the coffee brews at what is regarded as the perfect time and temperature for the best cup of Joe.

But be aware that this standard calls for using 2 tablespoons of ground coffee for each 5-ounce cup, which produces a very full-bodied, strong cup of coffee that is not to everyone's taste.

Brewing coffee at home does mean you'll have a lot of spent grounds around, but instead of putting them in the trash, there are plenty of ways you can reuse old coffee grounds.

Sources indicate that cup sizeKeep in mind that coffee-maker cups are the equivalent of 5 ounces, or an old-fashioned teacup that isn't filled to the brim, leaving room for milk. Most coffee mugs in use today hold upward of 8 ounces. Therefore, a typical 12-cup coffee maker brews enough coffee for about seven mugs at the most.

Recent findings suggest that what kind of carafe?Models with thermal carafes tend to be more expensive than those with glass carafes. You can bring thermal carafes to the table, where they'll keep coffee hot for refills. However, these carafes have narrow openings that are difficult to hand-wash, and most can't be cleaned in the dishwasher. However, thermal carafes are beneficial if you drink coffee throughout the day.

Recent findings suggest that milk frotherIf you prefer your coffee straight, you won’t be concerned about the milk frother option, although do consider that other household members or guests may prefer their coffee served with a smooth froth. Having a milk frother combined will also save you the matter of having a separate appliance on the countertop, taking up space.

Paper or permanent filters? Decide if you want to use a permanent filter or paper, disposable ones. Permanent filters are better for the environment, and you don't have to constantly replace them, but they do need to be thoroughly washed by hand and they tend to stain.

Also, it's easier to toss paper filters in the trash than knock grounds out of a metal filter. You may also find that the taste of the coffee produced differs depending on filter type and that you prefer one over the other.

According to recent reports, do you want to set it and forget it? With many machines, you can program them ahead of time to brew in the morning or right before you get home, and you can even set them to brew at the same time every day. But such features add to the price and work only if you take the time to read the manual and figure out how to use the setting.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for a drip coffee maker, one of the best indicators of quality is an SCA Gold Cup Standard certification. The SCA (Specialty Coffee Association) awards this to machines that brew a 1:16 to 1:18 ratio (that's parts coffee to water) and within a specific temperature range of 196 and 205 degrees Fahrenheit.

Typically, machines that meet this specification are ideally designed to deliver a good cup of coffee. Every drip machine within this guide is SCA-certified, too.

Looking for an espresso machine? Don't pay much attention to the number of bars of pressure it offers. Anything over nine will suffice, as this is the amount of pressure required to make espresso. Instead, consider the number of grind settings on any included grinders, as a quality grinder should allow for plenty of customization. For most people, an in-built PID controller will assist you in getting that perfect extraction.

If you're looking for a bean-to-cup coffee machine, you're likely in the market for a superautomatic, meaning you can press a button and it will grind and brew your drink using fully automatic internal systems.

Recent findings suggest that we've tested a number of bean-to-cup machines, and our top pick is the Terra Kafe Demi, which works fast and creates balanced, evenly-extracted brews. Its in-built milk frothing is also up to scratch if you enjoy a frothy coffee, although it'll never rival a hand-steamed latte.

If you want to create a range of milk-based espresso drinks, you should opt for something with a separate steam wand. I'd suggest you check out the Ninja Luxe Café Pro, which has a separate steam wand with both manual and automatic steaming.

Industry observers note that if you opt for automatic, the wand will texturize your milk to your desired level and according to the type of milk (dairy, oat, almond, etc) you choose. There's even a menu on the side of the machine which guides you through the different milk settings, and which to use depending on your desired drink.

My hot take is that you'll have a longer-lasting coffee setup if you opt for a separate brewer and one of the best coffee grinders, but if you want an in-built grinder, there are some good options out there.

Industry observers note that if you want an espresso machine, a quality grinder is especially notable, as your beans will need to be ground very finely to achieve a quality extraction. As a general rule, I trust Breville machines to grind well, and I also had a great experience with the "Bean Adapt" tech in the De'Longhi La Specialista Touch.

#142458. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (758 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
  • It has been revealed that it’s an exciting time for NASA.
  • Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It has been revealed that it’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

Industry observers note that these satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s Fresh Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the company was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their latest trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

Sources indicate that by the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally debuted Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a latest strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, remarked in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

That extra incentive to buy the stock has pushed it to newly introduced heights of over $1,100, with it now being up around 28% since the start of the year. Given its high value today, could a stock split be around the corner, and could that lead to further gains for shareholders?

Stock splits are rare events for Costco, and the last time one happened was back in early 2000. The company could have justified doing a stock split years ago when it had already risen north of $500. The higher its price goes, the more inevitable speculation there will be about a possible stock split taking place again.

However, it's a purely discretionary move for management that doesn't fundamentally make the business any better of a buy, nor does it improve the look of its financials. Shareholders own the same stake in the business before and immediately after a split. While the price may change, so too will the share count, adjusting based on the split size.

Recent findings suggest that and while a stock split is typically a good sign that the share price has risen significantly to the point that a stock split makes sense, that doesn't necessarily mean that it'll likely continue rising after a split. Valuation is also very key to consider, and Costco's stock just isn't cheap right now.

NASDAQ · As of 11:48 AM ET 11/23/26.

In five years, Costco's stock has doubled in value. But whether it can replicate that success in the next five years is a bit doubtful, as it's trading at more than 50 times its trailing earnings, which is a fairly rich valuation for a retail stock.

At this high a price, investors should tread carefully, as it may not take much for the stock to come down in value. A lot of bullishness is priced into its valuation, and while the business may be performing well, that doesn't mean the stock is a good buy at such a high price. The S&P 500, which is a collection of the leading stocks on U.S. markets, averages a price-to-earnings multiple of just over 20.

Costco's stock has done well in recent years, but investors should be careful as its future gains may be much more modest in light of its high valuation.

There are three main types of domestic espresso machines — manual, automatic, and superautomatic — and each is suited to a different type of buyer.
